There were only 35 units that were occupied at that time. A team of people got together, explored multiple redevelopment options, including let's build some affordable housing. They determined that the highest and the best use for that location would be commercial development. Property sold $2 million to a private developer. There was actually quite a bit of interest that was gained over that because it took about five years for all this to actually transpire. What Norman Affordable Housing Corporation did was they purchased multiple single family units that they rent at affordable rates. They look at household incomes, the composition of the households, and back into what is an affordable rate for households that are 80% below median income. With this, they have actually generated enough money through the collection of this rent that they have about $120,000 annually that they reinvest into projects with partnerships with us. This will be the fourth project that we have done with them. This project, our total development cost is $765,945, of which the Home Investment Partnership Program is providing $535,686, the CHOTO $118,134, and the Affordable Housing Corporation $112,125. The uses of those funds were the acquisition of the three lots, obviously the construction costs, and then to ensure the continued affordability of the property, we go ahead and fund the initial reserve replacement for these properties. That's just the property savings account that is a deposit made to each year by the manager to ensure that as things need replaced, such as appliances, roofs, things like that, that there is the capital money there to do that. So these properties, once the construction is completed, they'll be turned over to the Affordable Housing Corporation from the CHOTO. The CHOTO, as I said, is operating as the sponsor of this.
